summary: When astronauts travel into deep space, talking to mission control can take over 20 minutes—meaning they are completely on their own if a medical emergency hits. That is why we built KUXTAL, an autonomous web-based "pocket doctor" designed to keep crews safe on long-duration missions. With a quick 2-minute daily check-in, astronauts can log their vital signs and instantly see their health status translated onto an interactive human body map using clear, color-coded triage indicators (Green, Yellow, Red). Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, KUXTAL goes beyond simple tracking by integrating official frameworks like the NASA Human Research Roadmap (5 Hazards), NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1, live space weather updates from the NASA DONKI API, and CSA radiation monitoring resources. Ultimately, KUXTAL is designed to eliminate data fatigue, provide true medical independence in isolated environments, and catch environmental or physiological risks early before they become critical.
details:
KUXTAL is an autonomous, web-based "pocket doctor" designed to safeguard astronaut health on long-duration space missions. When crews travel into deep space, communicating with Earth can face delays of over 20 minutes, making real-time medical supervision from ground control impossible. KUXTAL solves this by empowering astronauts to perform rapid, 2-minute daily check-ins to log their key vital signs and mental wellbeing.

The system translates raw physiological data into an intuitive, interactive human body map. Using a clear color-coded triage system (Green for optimal, Yellow for attention, and Red for critical), it helps astronauts instantly identify health risks. Furthermore, KUXTAL adapts to different mission environments—such as a Lunar Base, the ISS, or Mars Transit—and integrates live space weather updates from the NASA DONKI API (tracking solar storms and radiation) to provide context-aware risk evaluations.

Our main goal is to eliminate data fatigue, prevent medical crises in isolated environments, and give astronauts true physiological and psychological independence. By catching health and environmental hazards early, KUXTAL ensures crew safety without burning out crew members with heavy or complicated software.

KUXTAL was built as an offline-first web prototype to ensure seamless performance even with intermittent connectivity in space. Our technical stack includes:

- JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, python, local Chart.js

- Official Data Frameworks: NASA Human Research Program (5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight), NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1, and CSA radiation resources.

Our code and proyect link: https://github.com/damamarquez151-wq/KUXTAL-/tree/main?tab=readme-ov-file
